Instead of subtracting the averaged distance vector, one can project the point onto each plane individually and then average the projected points.
- **Direction of update:** Subtracting the averaged vector moves the point towards the planes (convergence).
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot I)$, where $N$ is the number of intersecting edges per voxel and $I$ is the number of iterations.
Typically $N \le 12$ (max edges in a cube) and $I=5$, making it very fast per voxel.

- **When to use:** When performance is critical and normals are reliable.
Suitable for real-time applications or when QEF solving is too expensive.
- **When not to use:** When high geometric accuracy is required in the presence of noisy normals or non-intersecting planes.
